description: A sweeping view of the Nubian desert with the smaller, steeper pyramids of Meroe in the background. The sand is reddish-gold.
text_content: South of Egypt, in the land of Cush, a new kind of kingdom was born. This was a land of gold mines and strong warriors.

description: A dramatic low-angle shot of a Kushite King (pharaoh) wearing the distinct cap-crown with two cobras. He looks regal and powerful. Temple columns behind him.
text_content: The people of Cush were powerful. Once, their kings marched north and became the Pharaohs of Egypt! We call them the Black Pharaohs.

description: The city of Meroe at its height. Smoke rises from iron smelting furnaces. The city is bustling with trade and activity.
text_content: But their true home was the city of Meroe. Meroe was not just a city of stone; it was a city of fire and iron.

description: Close up of an ancient blacksmith striking glowing red iron on an anvil. Sparks fly. He is focused and skilled. Realistic detail.
text_content: The people learned the secret of smelting iron. They made strong tools for farming and sharp spears for hunting. Iron made them rich.

description: Queen Amanirenas leading her army into battle. She is fierce, riding a war chariot or horse, holding a spear. Roman soldiers are retreating in the distance.
text_content: Meroe was also famous for its Queens, called 'Kandakes'. When the Romans tried to attack, a one-eyed Queen named Amanirenas led her army to stop them!

description: A stone stele covered in Meroitic script. A scholar or scribe is carving into it. In the background, merchants trade ivory and cloth.
text_content: The Cushites wrote in their own special alphabet. They built temples and palaces. They traded with India and Arabia.

description: The Ethiopian Eunuch sitting in a grand chariot on a desert road. He is reading a scroll intently. Philip the Evangelist is approaching on foot.
text_content: One day, a man from Cush was riding his chariot home from Jerusalem. He was reading a scroll from the prophet Isaiah.

description: Philip baptizing the Ethiopian official in a small desert oasis pool. The official looks joyful and at peace. The chariot waits nearby.
text_content: God sent a man named Philip to explain the scroll. The man from Cush believed the good news about Jesus! He took that joy back to Africa.

description: King Ezana standing on a balcony of his palace in the highlands. He holds a coin with a Cross on it, showing it to the people.
text_content: Later, a new kingdom called Aksum grew in the mountains. A King named Ezana decided to follow Jesus, too.

description: Ruins of the Meroe pyramids under a starry night sky. The Milky Way is visible. The scene is quiet and majestic.
text_content: The fires of Meroe eventually went out, but the history of the Iron Kingdom shows us the strength and skill of Africa's ancient people.

description: A montage spread showing an iron spearhead, a gold bracelet, and a piece of pottery from Meroe. Artifacts on a museum table.
text_content: They were builders, warriors, and believers. Their story is written in the iron and the stone.

description: A parchment map of the varying Nile cataracts (waterfalls). It marks 'Meroe', 'Napata', and 'Aksum'. The Red Sea trade routes are dotted lines.
text_content: Map: The Land of the Bow. This map shows the Nile bending in an 'S' shape. The city of Meroe is between the rivers. The Red Sea is to the East.
